Consumers use the extended type guard rather than matching provider IDs. Provider-neutral features continue to depend on `ISessionsProvider`.

+Operations that need a running chat's configuration independently of visibility use `acquireSessionConfig` with the exact chat resource and dispose the lease afterward. The provider retains and awaits the session and applicable chat configuration subscriptions, rejecting missing or failed state instead of substituting parent permissions; cancellation, connection loss, and provider disposal release pending leases. New-session capabilities are resolved with `resolveSessionConfigForCreation` for the target workspace and harness, not inferred from an existing parent session's schema.

Session configuration is discovered before client defaults are sent. The existing approval and repository controls select one validated schema binding and retain its original property names and enum values for completions, draft creation, and runtime changes. A published VS Code key selects the VS Code convention even when malformed, in which case the property uses generic UI rather than falling through to another host's convention. Copilot `approvalMode` is a requested preference; its read-only `effectiveApprovalMode` and `availableApprovalModes` report the effective posture and selectable choices, without granting tool permissions in the client. Copilot `target` maps workspace/worktree presentation, `baseBranch` selects the base branch, and `branch` names the new branch. Unsupported defaults, read-only reports, and non-mutable runtime properties are not client writes.

When a host supplies the optional `vscode.modelConfiguration` read-only session report, entries are keyed by the exact advertised chat URI. The content provider maps only that chat's model identifiers to editor identifiers and exposes the report through `IChatSession.modelConfigurationState` and `IChatModel.modelConfigurationState`. The shared chat input uses its defaults, read-only options, and applied values without overwriting personal preferences or another chat's state. Absence or removal clears the scoped projection; runtime ownership and enforcement do not move into the client. Host-advertised `vscode.modelConfiguration.defaults` model metadata opts model options into scalar source tracking so an untouched displayed default is not mistaken for an explicit selection when it crosses AHP.
